trial.title: Double-Dose Third-Generation EGFR-TKI Plus Bevacizumab and Intrathecal Chemotherapy for Refractory Leptomeningeal Metastatic NSCLC: A Phase II Study
indication: Lung Neoplasms, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

endpoints.time_frame: Up to 30 days after the last study drug administration (for safety and response assessment), and through study completion, an average of 1 years (for survival follow-up)
endpoints.description: The primary endpoint is leptomeningeal metastasis overall response rate (LM-ORR) evaluated by RANO-LM criteria.

outcome.rationale: Triple combination addresses LM through complementary mechanisms with strong biological rationale. Historical data support each component: osimertinib 160mg (LM-ORR 62%), intrathecal pemetrexed (DCR 88.8%). Predicted LM-ORR 55% likely meets Phase II efficacy threshold for refractory LM. Key risks: small sample, no comparator, heterogeneous TKI selection.

value.uncertainty: No direct Phase II data for exact triple combination; based on BLOOM monotherapy (62% ORR) and intrathecal pemetrexed retrospective data (88.8% DCR). Wide CI reflects single-arm design, small sample, and heterogeneity in TKI selection.
value.rationale: Triple combination builds on proven mechanisms: double-dose TKI achieves adequate CSF concentration (BLOOM: 62% ORR), bevacizumab enhances CNS drug delivery, intrathecal pemetrexed provides direct CSF cytotoxicity (retrospective DCR 88.8%). Predicted LM-ORR 55% (95% CI 38-72%) based on additive effects, tempered by heavily pretreated population and acquired resistance.

analysis_trace.finding: Phase II single-arm study evaluating double-dose third-generation EGFR-TKI (osimertinib 160mg, furmonertinib 160mg, or almonertinib 220mg) plus bevacizumab and intrathecal pemetrexed for EGFR-mutant NSCLC with leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) after prior EGFR-TKI failure. Primary endpoint: LM-ORR by RANO-LM criteria. N=30, recruiting, expected completion 2027-12-30.
Refractory LM after first-/second-/third-generation EGFR-TKI progression. ECOG 0-1. Heavily pretreated population with poor prognosis (historical median OS ~3 months without effective therapy).

Triple combination: (1) Double-dose third-gen EGFR-TKI for enhanced CNS penetration and overcoming resistance; (2) Bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) to improve blood-brain barrier permeability and reduce edema; (3) Intrathecal pemetrexed for direct CSF drug delivery. Synergistic rationale supported by preclinical and early clinical data.

LM-ORR (leptomeningeal metastasis overall response rate) assessed by RANO-LM criteria combines neurological exam, CSF cytology, and MRI. Requires complete/partial response per standardized criteria. Single-arm design without comparator.

Key evidence: (1) BLOOM study (osimertinib 160mg): LM-ORR 62% in T790M+ LM patients; (2) Intrathecal pemetrexed retrospective study (Yao 2025): DCR 88.8%, median OS 8.15 months; (3) Furmonertinib + bevacizumab + intrathecal pemetrexed real-world data (ASCO 2025): remarkable efficacy in similar population. Triple combination rationale is sound with additive/synergistic mechanisms.

Expected toxicities: myelosuppression (40% Grade ≥3 in intrathecal pemetrexed studies), hypertension (bevacizumab), EGFR-TKI-related skin toxicity, diarrhea. Dose reductions may be needed (furmonertinib reduced to 160mg in some patients per ASCO abstract). Manageable with supportive care.

1) Small single-arm study (N=30) with no comparator; 2) Heterogeneous TKI selection (osimertinib/furmonertinib/almonertinib) may confound results; 3) Heavily pretreated population with acquired resistance mechanisms; 4) Intrathecal therapy requires invasive administration (lumbar puncture/Ommaya); 5) RANO-LM criteria inter-observer variability.

No direct Phase II data for exact triple combination with double-dose TKI. Limited published data on almonertinib in LM. Most evidence from retrospective studies or case series. No randomized comparator data available.
